convertibility_reason: Uses iCustom('UltraWPR') which is a custom indicator with multi-layer smoothing (JJMA/JurX/ParMA/T3/VIDYA/AMA) from external SmoothAlgorithms.mqh library, plus TradeAlgorithms.mqh for order management. The custom indicator and its smoothing algorithms require manual Python reimplementation.

custom_logic_notes: The UltraWPR indicator applies multi-stage adaptive smoothing to WPR: first an adaptive variable-period MA (JJMA with xStep/xStepsTotal creating multiple smoothed versions), then a final smoothing pass. This is not a simple WPR crossover - it's a heavily filtered/smoothed WPR with crossover of two smoothed lines (UpValue from buffer 0, DnValue from buffer 1). Signal detection requires UpValue[1]>DnValue[1] (trend established on previous bar) AND UpValue[0]<=DnValue[0] (crossover just happened on signal bar). The BuyPosOpen/SellPosOpen/BuyPosClose/SellPosClose input booleans act as gates. SignalBar=1 means signals are read 1 bar back, adding confirmation delay. TradeAlgorithms.mqh provides BuyPositionOpen/SellPositionOpen/BuyPositionClose/SellPositionClose with time-based duplicate trade prevention (UpSignalTime/DnSignalTime).
external_dependencies: SmoothAlgorithms.mqh - Contains CXMA class and smoothing methods (JJMA, JurX, ParMA, T3, VIDYA, AMA, SMA, EMA, SMMA, LWMA)
TradeAlgorithms.mqh - Contains BuyPositionOpen, SellPositionOpen, BuyPositionClose, SellPositionClose, LoadHistory, CIsNewBar, GlobalVariableDel_
python_conversion_notes: Must reimplement the UltraWPR custom indicator: (1) standard WPR with period 13, (2) adaptive variable-period smoothing using JJMA algorithm with period stepping from StartLength to StartLength+xStep*xStepsTotal in steps of xStep, then (3) a second JJMA smoothing pass with period SmoothLength. The JJMA (JMA/Jurik) algorithm is not trivial - consider using the 'jma' Python package or implementing from the SmoothAlgorithms.mqh source. Alternatively, approximate with EMA if exact replication is not required. The TradeAlgorithms.mqh order management can be replaced with simple market order logic since the core is just crossover entry with fixed SL/TP. Key: buffers 0 and 1 of UltraWPR represent two smoothed WPR lines whose crossover generates signals.
